summary: Lake County, MT lookout: a 50-foot pole L-4 tower built 1936, abandoned 1964 and destroyed about 1966; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Destroyed about 1966 per firelookout.com; Forest Lookouts says removed, undated

events.note: A lookout reported five fires in August 1959 that could not be found; the next day the same lookout reported the same fires
Reported fires traced to reflections of Swan Lake town lights; account credited to the Independent Record

evidence.supports: location about 14 miles northeast of Polson, Lake County
agencies listed as Flathead National Forest and Montana DNRC
built 1936 as a 50-foot pole L-4 tower

was abandoned in 1964, and destroyed about 1966

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1959 account calls the lookout 'Woodward peak'; the page heading and other sources say Woodward Point. Treated as one site because Forest Lookouts files the account under Woodward Point.
Forest Lookouts says 'Removed' with no date; Rex Kamstra says destroyed about 1966. Both agree the tower is gone.

notes_for_editor: Only three pages read; Kamstra and Kemnow are hobby sites, and the 1936 build date and 1966 destruction come from Kamstra alone. The brief's agency (Flathead National Forest) omits the Montana DNRC named on Kamstra's page; left as is. Kamstra's page mentions a Fire Lookout Museum photo but gives no image URL, so no photo added. No source describes what remains at the site or public access; brief access 'unknown' kept. Staffing facts omitted: the 1959 account names no staffing status.
